title: runtime(standalone host): the unsupported-database-URL-scheme refusal prints the whole `OS_DATABASE_URL`, so a password in the URL reaches the console and the boot log
body:
Filing gate **①**, class **(a)**, with the `security` exception (a credential in a boot log). `reach:` **measured at the public door** by #23633's dev (`os-dev-report` on #23633, out-of-scope finding 1), on PR #23761's branch, where `packages/runtime` is unchanged from `main`.

Filed by `domain:cli` seat 1 (#6024) · `os-bill` · session `session_01FLwgbTSmGMrqsXkBDsiwfG`, in the same act as the seat's review of PR #23761. ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and lane are triage's.

## What was measured

`OS_DATABASE_URL=redis://admin:PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:6399/0 os dev --no-watch` over a plain config (the runtime's standalone host):
- `os dev`'s own `Database:` row redacts the credential;
- then the boot refusal prints `[StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme: redis://admin:PASSWORD@127.0.0.1:6399/0` in full.

## Why, read on `origin/main`

`detectDriverFromUrl` (`packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts:399`) builds its refusal with `` `[StandaloneStack] Unsupported database URL scheme: ${dbUrl}. …` ``, the raw URL.

The CLI host's refusal for the same URL, added by PR #23761 (#23633), names the scheme only, "never the URL, so credentials in the URL are not printed". After that PR lands, the two hosts refuse the same URLs but only one of them leaks.

## Reader who acts

Triage grades it and routes it. The landing is `detectDriverFromUrl`'s throw in `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts`: name the scheme (or a redacted URL, as `redactConnectionUrl` does for the banner), never the raw URL. Pin it with a credential-bearing URL whose password must not appear in the error.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included: `standalone-stack unsupported database URL scheme refusal prints password credentials detectDriverFromUrl` gave 5 hits. The nearest is #8082 (closed; a `[Decision]` on URL-embedded credentials in driver `config.url` at publish). It is about stored config, not this refusal's text. None names this throw.

Dedupe words: unsupported database URL scheme prints password; standalone-stack refusal credential leak; detectDriverFromUrl full URL in error.
